rationale: Apparent variant of ⲛⲟⲁⲙ 'power/might' (in glossary) with prosthetic ⲟ-, or compound ⲟⲩⲛ̄-ⲟⲁⲙ 'there is power.' Found in line 1 paralleled in line 4 ⲡⲉϩⲟⲛ̄ⲟⲁⲙ 'his power.' Confidence low pending parallels.
Obscure lexeme in line 3, in context of king moving something among his satraps. Possibly Lyc. abbreviation of ⲡⲉϥ-ⲟⲩⲉϩⲥⲁϩⲛⲉ 'his command' or related to ⲱⲧⲡ̄/ⲱⲧⲏ. Confidence low.

proposed_english: to bear (under the kings) / be subjected
rationale: Verb ⲃⲓ 'carry, bear' here used idiomatically with ⲍⲁ 'under' to mean 'be subjected to.' The combined sense ⲃⲓ ⲍⲁ ⲛ̄ⲣⲣⲟ = 'bear (the yoke) under the kings' = 'be a subject of the kings.'

proposed_english: he received upon him / took to himself
rationale: Lyc. ⲁⲭⲓ = ⲁϥϫⲓ '3sg.m took/received'; with ⲁⲣⲁϩ 'upon him' (reflexive) yields 'received upon himself.' Standard Coptic idiom for accepting/taking on something.

Sasanian province at the head of the Persian Gulf (Greek Mesene, Middle Persian Mēšān). Standard Manichaean missionary station; Mani's first major mission outside Persia proper, traditionally located here.
